investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota or physical VM slots are exhausted), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 124–148 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Most likely — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or leaked/zombie pods that were not cleaned up, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Swarm Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm cluster was left unscheduled — the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes (peer-pod VM slots are full), and the remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. This prevents any new remote-agent pod from being scheduled, which causes the eval runner's createAgent step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1364) to block until the probe timeout fires. Because the agent is never created, the state-polling step that follows never executes, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) remain absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota or physical VM slots are exhausted), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 124–148 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Most likely — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or leaked/zombie pods that were not cleaned up, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a node label or taint that only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are simultaneously at VM capacity, creating a combined capacity+affinity bottleneck.

Cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM slot capacity relative to concurrent eval or production workload demand at the time of the run (2026-06-17T18:35–18:43Z).

Leaked remote agent pods from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) holding VM slots and preventing new scheduling — possible if cleanup failed silently in a previous run.

Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes (peer-pod VM slots are full), and the remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. This prevents any new remote-agent pod from being scheduled, which causes the eval runner's createAgent step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1364) to block until the probe timeout fires. Because the agent is never created, the state-polling step that follows never executes, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) remain absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
